info.title: ThinnestAI API
info.description: Build voice and WhatsApp agents, place calls, message customers and run a platform of your own customers on one API.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: An agent is one assistant with its instructions, model, languages, website widget and call settings — the same thing the console's Agent page builds. Create one here, then give it knowledge, actions and channels.

tags.name: Knowledge
tags.description: The documents an agent searches and cites when it answers — a web page or pasted text, split into passages and indexed. Use it for facts (prices, policies, opening hours) rather than putting them in the instructions.

tags.name: Actions
tags.description: Calls to your own HTTPS API that an agent can make mid-conversation, with arguments it fills from what the customer said — how an agent uses data that stays in your own system. Create one, test it, then switch it on.

tags.name: Tools
tags.description: Everything else an agent can do besides answer: its built-in tools, the MCP tool servers it is connected to, and the accounts it works in (calendar, spreadsheets, CRMs, records kept here, helpdesks). Every tool starts off.

tags.name: Channels
tags.description: Where an agent answers: the website widget, WhatsApp, Telegram and calls. Read an agent's channels here and connect a Telegram bot; WhatsApp is connected in the console, because Meta's sign-up runs in the business owner's own browser.

tags.name: Calls
tags.description: A call is one phone, web or WhatsApp conversation with an agent — one you placed through the API, a campaign's, or one a customer made to you. Place calls here, one at a time or in a batch, and read each one back with its summary, collected details and transcript.

tags.name: Post-call
tags.description: What happens after a call ends: the outcome, a short summary and the details the agent collects. Read a call's analysis here, and set what an agent does after every call.

tags.name: Recordings
tags.description: A call's audio, for agents that record their calls. Fetch it with your key, or hand a CRM user the signed link a call report carries — that one needs no key.

tags.name: Conversations
tags.description: A conversation is one customer's thread with your workspace on one channel — WhatsApp, the web widget, Telegram, voice or email. Read threads and their messages (including to catch up on a webhook you missed), answer a WhatsApp customer from your own agent platform, and resolve, take over or assign threads as the inbox does.

tags.name: Messages
tags.description: Send one approved WhatsApp template to one customer, because something happened in your own system — an order confirmation, a delivery update, an appointment reminder. No agent is needed: this is how your software starts a WhatsApp conversation.

tags.name: One-time codes
tags.description: Deliver a login or verification code you generated over WhatsApp, without handling templates yourself, and set up the authentication templates it sends with. WhatsApp writes these messages — "*394812* is your verification code." — so you choose only the expiry, the security line and the button.

tags.name: Contacts
tags.description: The people your workspace knows — kept in step with your CRM by phone number and your own `externalId`, with marketing consent recorded alongside where it came from.

tags.name: Do not call
tags.description: Numbers your agents must never ring. Every outbound call refuses a number on this list — Create Call answers `409`, a batch refuses that entry, a calling campaign skips the person and records why, and a booked callback is given up — while inbound calls from it are answered as usual. The same list as **Contacts → Do not contact** in the console, and the one your voice agent adds to on its own when a caller asks not to be called again (in any language), which also sends the `contact.opted_out` webhook event.

tags.name: Events
tags.description: Tell us something happened in your system — `order.delivered`, `trial.ended` — and the sequences and tags you set up in the console decide what follows. Your code says what happened; the console says what happens next.

tags.name: Templates
tags.description: WhatsApp message templates: the pre-approved messages your business may send to a customer first, or outside the 24 hours after they last wrote. A template is saved as a draft, sent to WhatsApp for review, and can be sent (Send Message, Create Campaign) only once it is `approved`. Templates are named, not numbered, and one name can exist in several languages.

tags.name: Campaigns
tags.description: A campaign sends one thing to many people. It is either a WhatsApp **broadcast** (`kind: "whatsapp"`), which sends one approved template to everyone in its audience, or a **calling campaign** (`kind: "voice"`), where an agent phones each person from its own number within the hours you set. Who is in the audience is decided by consent, exactly as in the console, and every campaign is created as a draft that you then launch, schedule, pause, resume or cancel.

tags.name: Sequences
tags.description: A sequence sends one person several approved WhatsApp templates over days — "your order shipped", then "how was it?" two days later — and stops by itself when they reply, are tagged, or an event says so. People join by tag, by event, or one at a time through Enrol in Sequence. Sequence ids are bare uuids.

tags.name: Forms
tags.description: A WhatsApp form is a screen your customer fills in without leaving the chat — a delivery address, an appointment request, a short survey. Build it here, publish it to your own WhatsApp Business Account, then send it from a template's button, an agent, the inbox or Reply to Conversation.

tags.name: Phone numbers
tags.description: The numbers your agents answer and call from. A workspace holds them two ways: numbers it **rents** here, charged every month from your balance, and numbers it **brings** from its own carrier account, which we never bill. Each number is answered by at most one agent (its line) and may be lent to one agent to call out on. A number is named by the number itself, in any spelling: `918041234567`, `+918041234567` and `%2B918041234567` in a path are the same number.

tags.name: SMS
tags.description: Your own SMS provider and your own DLT registration, so your agents can text customers in India — during a call (the `send_sms` built-in tool) and after it (an agent's post-call `followUp`). Every business SMS in India must match a template approved on your DLT portal and go out under your six-letter sender header; your provider bills you for each one, and nothing is charged to your wallet here. Providers: `msg91`, `exotel`, `gupshup` (Enterprise SMS), `infobip`, `vonage`, `fast2sms`. On your DLT portal, add your provider as your telemarketer (the PE–TM chain) or every send is rejected.

tags.name: Voices
tags.description: The voices an agent can speak with, as the console's voice picker lists them. An item's `id` is what an agent's `voice.voice` takes.

tags.name: Voice clones
tags.description: Your workspace's own cloned voices, made from a short recording with the speaker's consent. A clone is listed with the Studio voices and can be put on an agent like any other voice.

tags.name: Models
tags.description: The language models an agent can answer with, as the console names them. An item's `id` is what an agent's `model` takes.

tags.name: Bring your own keys
tags.description: Run your agents on your own provider accounts and pay a flat platform fee instead of our usage rates. Bring all three keys (speech-to-text, LLM, voice): ₹0.02 a chat reply and ₹1 a call minute, all-in. Or bring only your voice key (scope voice): our speech-to-text, model and telephony, a call billed at the voice-only BYOK rate (₹1.50 / $0.02 a minute by default), which includes our model — so calls run only on Prana, Prana [Voice], GPT-OSS 120B or another model GET /api/v1/models marks `voiceOnlyByok` (an agent on any other model runs on Prana on calls) — chat replies as usual, on any model. Or bring your language-model key and your voice key (scope llm_voice): we keep the speech recogniser, a call is a flat ₹1 a minute like all three keys, with no model limit, and a chat reply is the same flat fee. Or bring only your language-model key (scope llm): we keep the speech recogniser and the voice, and a call is billed exactly like any other call on the voice plan the agent speaks with — Premium or Studio — whatever model your key runs, with no model limit; chat replies are billed at the same flat own-keys fee as under all three keys. There is no fallback to our providers when one of your keys fails. The switch and the default `scope` are per workspace, and each agent follows them by default. Each agent can choose for itself (Create Agent, Update Agent `byok`): `null` follows the workspace, `"off"` runs that one agent on our voices and models at our normal pricing — chat replies billed normally, the voice-only model limit not applied — and a scope (`all`, `voice`, `llm` or `llm_voice`) runs it on that scope's keys, so one workspace with an LLM key and a voice key can have one agent on `llm` and another on `llm_voice`. A scope is refused (409, naming the missing key) unless you hold verified keys for it, and a key an agent's scope needs cannot be removed while BYOK is on. If a key is gone when a call starts, the agent falls back to the workspace's scope, never fails the call. A call is priced and run on one stack: the agent's setting is read once when the call or reply starts.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Endpoints an agent's events are sent to as they happen — a CRM, a sheet, Slack, Zapier, or a helpdesk email address. Each delivery is a signed JSON `POST` of `{ "id", "event", "sentAt", "data" }`.

**Headers on every attempt** (not sent to an email destination, which gets one ticket email per event)

| Header | What it is |
|---|---|
| `x-thinnest-signature` | `sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body>` under the endpoint's signing secret. |
| `x-thinnest-signature-v2` | `sha256=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<x-thinnest-delivered-at>.<raw body>">` — the delivery time, signed. |
| `x-thinnest-delivered-at` | When this attempt left (ISO 8601). |
| `x-thinnest-event-id` | `evt_…`, the same as the body's `id` — stable across every retry and re-send. |
| `x-thinnest-attempt` | `1` for the first attempt, then `2`, `3`, … |

**Retries.** A delivery that fails — any answer other than 2xx, a timeout after 10 seconds, or an address we cannot reach — is tried again after 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 6 hours (six attempts over about 8½ hours). Every attempt sends the **same bytes**, so `sentAt` is when the event happened, not when the attempt left. Payloads are kept for 7 days; within that time any failed delivery can be sent again with Redeliver Webhook Events.

**Dedupe** on `x-thinnest-event-id` (or the body's `id`): a retry after a timeout can reach you after you already processed the first attempt. Answer 2xx quickly and do the work afterwards.

**Freshness.** To refuse replayed requests, verify `x-thinnest-signature-v2` and reject an `x-thinnest-delivered-at` more than five minutes from your clock. Do not check freshness on `sentAt`: a retry's `sentAt` is hours old by design.

**Switch-off.** An endpoint is switched off after five events in a row that each failed every attempt — single failed attempts that later succeed do not count. Events that happen while it is off are recorded as not sent; switch it back on and re-send them.

**Ids in `data`** are the prefixed ids the API returns and takes: `conversationId` is `conv_…` (the conversation endpoints take it), `campaignId` is `cmp_…`, and a call is `out_…`, `sch_…` or its call reference (Get Call takes it). The `WebhookPayload` schema has a full example of every event's body.

The events an endpoint can subscribe to:

| Event | When it fires |
|---|---|
| `lead.captured` | The agent collected a name, email or phone from somebody who showed real interest. |
| `conversation.escalated` | The agent handed a conversation to a person — asked for, or because it could not answer. |
| `conversation.resolved` | A teammate marked a conversation done. |
| `call.completed` | A call the agent placed or answered ended — how it ended and how long it lasted, sent the moment it ends. |
| `call.analysed` | A call's results are ready: its summary, the details it collected, how it went and what comes next (`insights`, when the agent's Call insights is on), the transcript, a recording link and what the call cost (`costMicro`, `currency`) — the same shape as Get Call. |
| `campaign.finished` | Every person on a broadcast or a calling campaign has been reached, or given up on. |
| `contact.opted_out` | During a call, somebody asked not to be called again; their number (`data.phone`) is now on the do-not-call list; `data.source` is `"call"`; `data.reason` is the words they used, as recorded, or null. |
| `call.problem` | During a call: the agent could not answer, your own model key failed, a reply was very slow, or the voice connection failed. Sent once per kind per call. |
| `contact.erased` | A contact you deleted is gone completely, recordings included — at once, or after the nightly retry when a recording could not be deleted straight away (`recordingsPending`). Sent once. |
| `byok.changed` | Your own keys changed: a key was added, replaced, removed or failed its check, or your own keys were switched on or off or set to cover different jobs. |

**`call.problem`** is sent while the call is still going on, at most once per kind per call: `data` is `{ "callId", "agentId", "kind", "detail", "at" }`, where `callId` is the id Get Call takes and `kind` is `no_answer_from_model` (the agent could not get an answer and apologised to the caller), `byok_failed` (your own model key failed), `slow_reply` (a reply took more than 5 seconds to start) or `voice_failed` (the call's voice connection failed). `detail` is a sentence to show a person.

**Calls handed to another agent.** `lead.captured` and `conversation.escalated` carry `data.agentId` (the agent that ran the tool) and `data.callId` (the id Get Call takes; null off a call). On a call handed to another agent the call-level events — `call.completed`, `call.analysed`, `call.problem` — stay with the agent the call started with, and `handedTo` on `call.analysed` and Get Call lists the others, so `callId` joins them. Each `handedTo` entry says whether the hand-off was `warm` or `cold` (`mode`) and, when warm, the `summary` the next agent was given. A hand-off to another agent is not a hand-over to a person and sends no `conversation.escalated`.

**Usage and billing per call.** `call.analysed` carries `data.usage` and `data.billing`, the same objects as Get Call's: `inputTokens`, `outputTokens` and `cachedInputTokens` the call's replies used (your own model key's too), `inputTokensEstimated` (true when part of the input count was estimated because the provider reported none) and `ttsCharacters` (text sent to the voice, including text sent before the caller interrupted); and `billing` — whose keys the call ran on (`keys`), the voice plan it was priced on (`voicePlan`), its per-minute rate (`ratePerMinuteMicro`) and the seconds it was charged for (`billedSeconds`).

**Workspace events.** `contact.erased` and `byok.changed` are about the whole workspace, not one agent. They go to every endpoint in the workspace that subscribed to them, whichever agent it was added on — once per address, so three agents posting to the same URL still receive one delivery — and to a developer's every-customer endpoints (`includeCustomers`) for an event in one of its customers. An endpoint subscribed to every event (`["*"]`) receives them too. Neither carries personal data or key material:

- `contact.erased`: `data` is `{ "contactId", "erasedAt" }` — the `cust_…` id Delete Contact was given and when it was erased. Sent exactly once: straight after Delete Contact when it answered 204, or from the nightly retry once the last recording it reported as `recordingsPending` is gone (a recording still being written can take up to three nights to be confirmed).
- `byok.changed`: `data` is `{ "change", "kind", "provider", "byokEnabled", "scope" }`. `change` is `key_added`, `key_replaced`, `key_removed`, `key_failed_verification` (the provider refused a key you tried to save; nothing was saved), `byok_enabled`, `byok_disabled` or `scope_changed`. `kind` (`stt`, `llm` or `tts`) and `provider` name the key for the four key changes and are null for the others. `byokEnabled` and `scope` are where the workspace stands after the change. A change of a key's model is not sent, and saved keys are not re-checked on a schedule: a model key that stops working on a call shows up as `call.problem` (`byok_failed`).

**Call quality.** `call.completed` and `call.analysed` carry `data.quality`, the same object as Get Call's `quality`: reply times (`responseMs` from the caller falling silent to the agent's first audio, `answerMs` to the first word of the actual answer, `firstTokenMs` our side of it — each median, p90 and max in milliseconds), long silences, interruptions, the turns that looked something up in the agent's knowledge (`knowledgeTurns`), and the turns the agent apologised for (`modelErrors`) or a backup model answered (`rescues`). It is null for a call that was not measured, and on `call.completed` when the call ended before its figures arrived — `call.analysed` and Get Call have them by then.

tags.name: Usage
tags.description: Read what your workspace used and spent — replies, calls, WhatsApp, the balance history and invoices — the same figures as the console's Usage and Billing pages. All reads.

tags.name: Analytics
tags.description: The Dashboard's counts and each agent's Analytics page, for building a dashboard of your own that agrees with the console.

tags.name: Customers
tags.description: Workspaces you create for your own customers when you build a product on this API. Each customer has its own agents, contacts, knowledge, phone numbers and WhatsApp; your one key reaches any of them by adding `Thinnest-Workspace: <customer id>` to a request, and everything they use is charged to you. Manage customers from your own workspace, without that header.

tags.name: Workspace
tags.description: Your workspace's own settings — its name and time zone — as Settings → General shows them. With `Thinnest-Workspace`, the customer's workspace instead.

tags.name: Projects
tags.description: Projects group a workspace's agents, and are what a team's access is scoped by. Every workspace has a default project that cannot be deleted; a second project needs a plan with teams and projects.

tags.name: Teams
tags.description: Teams are groups of members and the projects they can reach. A project granted to no team is open to the whole workspace; granting it to a team restricts it to that team's members (owners and admins always see everything), and removing its last grant opens it up again.

tags.name: Members
tags.description: The people in your workspace and their roles. An API key acts as an admin, never an owner: it can make people admins or members and remove them, but cannot make anybody an owner, and the last owner can be neither demoted nor removed.

tags.name: Invitations
tags.description: Invitations to join your workspace, as Settings → Members sends them: an email with a link that works for 14 days. Pending invitations count towards your plan's seats.

tags.name: Notifications
tags.description: What each kind of notification does in your workspace: shown in the console's feed or muted, and whether it is emailed through the email sender you connected in the console.

tags.name: Saved replies
tags.description: Sentences your team sends often, offered in the inbox composer as `/shortcut`.

tags.name: Contact groups
tags.description: Named lists of contacts — "Wholesale buyers", "Pune walk-ins" — the same groups as **Contacts → Groups** in the console. Aim a broadcast or a calling campaign at one with `groups` on Create Campaign. A group narrows who a campaign reaches and never widens it: consent still decides, exactly as for tags. Deleting a group never deletes its contacts. List a group's contacts with List Contacts and `group=grp_…`.

tags.name: Workflows
tags.description: Journeys run once per contact: calls, WhatsApp and SMS, waits, checks and AI decisions, built on the Workflows page. Start one for a contact from your own system.

delete.description:
Deletes the agent and everything under it: its conversations, knowledge, actions and channels. It cannot be undone. A **build** key may do this.

Refused with `409` `agent_on_live_call` while the agent is on a call (ringing or connected): deleting it then would lose that call's recording, transcript, analysis and usage. Delete it after the call ends.

Chooses the voice this agent speaks with on your own voice provider: an id from List BYOK Voices, checked against the provider's list for your key, or `null` for the provider's default. On Cartesia an id that is not on the list yet, such as a voice cloned a moment ago, is checked with Cartesia directly and accepted if your key owns it. The agent needs a voice channel first. get.description:
Where the time went in each turn of one call. Every time is in milliseconds from the moment the caller stopped speaking, so a turn reads as a row of steps: the recogniser's wait and the caller's final words, Ear's check, the turn being decided, the model being asked, the first words of the answer leaving the model, the first sound of any kind, and the answer being heard. `split` adds up the pieces a team works on: the wait before the turn was decided, the recogniser, Ear's check, the model's first sentence and the voice.

`answerAudioMs` is the time to the first word of the ACTUAL answer. `quality.responseMs` stops at the first sound of any kind, so a thinking line that plays first ends it; here `firstAudioKind` says what spoke first (`answer`, `filler` or `other`) and `answerAudioEstimated` is true when a filler spoke first and the answer's start is worked out from the audio queued behind it rather than heard directly. A step that did not happen on a turn is null, never zero. A negative `modelAskedMs` is real: with `earlyAnswers` the model is asked before the turn is decided.

`timeline` is null for a call that has none: a call from before this existed, or one on a call type that does not record it. It holds times only, no words, so it stays when a call's content is deleted. Any id List Calls hands out works.

Deletes ONE call's recording and transcript, and keeps its billing record. Gone: the recording (ours, the phone provider's copy of a call on a number we rent, and any copy made for model training), this call's own turns in its conversation (other calls and chats with the same person stay), its summary, its collected fields, and the summary handed on with a warm hand-off. Afterwards Get Call answers with `recording: null`, an empty `transcript`, `contentDeleted: true` and `contentDeletedAt`. A recording that cannot be deleted at that moment is queued and retried every night until it is gone, and counted in `recordingsPending`. For a call you placed that was retried, every attempt's content goes. This cannot be undone.

This is not Cancel Call: `DELETE /calls/{id}` still calls a call off. Safe to repeat — again answers 200 with the first deletion's time. Needs a **full** key; a developer reaches a customer's call with `Thinnest-Workspace`.

delete.description:
**Erases** the contact: their conversations and transcripts, their calls, any queued call and their campaign rows go with them, and so does any duplicate that was merged into them. This cannot be undone. Use it for a person's request to be forgotten; to stop messaging someone, set their consent to `withdrawn` instead. A **build** key may do this.

**Recordings are erased too.** The audio of their calls is deleted before the call rows go: a recording we store is deleted right away, the phone provider's copy of a call on a number we rent is deleted through your workspace's own account with them, and any copy made for model training is deleted. A file that cannot be deleted at that moment is queued and retried every night until it is gone; the contact is erased regardless, and the response says how many are still queued in `recordingsPending`.

**Knowing when it is finished.** Subscribe a webhook to `contact.erased`: it is sent once the erasure is complete — straight away when this answers 204, or from the nightly retry once the last queued recording is gone — with only the contact's id and when it was erased.

**What is not erased.** Do-not-call entries are kept deliberately, so the person is not called again. Webhook payloads we already sent are purged on their own schedule after 7 days. Copies in your own systems, and in your vendors', are yours to delete.

Moves a number, **keeping its digits**, from the workspace the request runs in to another workspace of the same developer: the developer's own, or any of its customers. Agent.description: An agent as the console shows it.

name.description: The agent's name, 2 to 60 characters.

instructions.description: What the agent is and how it behaves — its standing prompt.

greeting.description: The first thing it says, or an empty string.

businessDescription.description: One line about the business, or an empty string.

model.description: A model id from List Models. `null` when the agent is on a model that has since been retired.

maxReplyTokens.description: The longest a reply may be, in tokens — one ceiling for chat and calls.

language.description: `auto` (reply in the customer's language) or the language it always replies in, e.g. `Hindi`. When the agent is set to speak several languages this is `auto`: read `languages`.

languages.description: The languages the agent speaks, as the console shows them: `[]` is auto, one name is that language alone, and two to four are the languages it expects, the first being the one it falls back to.

secondLanguage.description: Retired — always `null`. An agent answers in one language, `language`. Still returned so a client that reads it keeps working.

captureLeads.description: Whether it takes a name, email or phone number from an interested customer.

ownRules.description: true leaves out the platform's own lead, hand-over and call-back sentences, for a business that writes those rules in its instructions. Left out: the sentence about asking for details (or that the business does not collect them), the hand-over rule (or that nobody can be handed to, and that nobody should promise a follow-up) and the "cannot book a call back" sentence. Kept whatever you send: the boundary, the AI disclosure, the reply language, the date, your own instructions, and how a call is put through to a person.

scheduleCallbacks.description: Whether it may book a call back when asked.

voice.description: How it handles calls. `null` when the agent has no voice channel (a deployment without voice).

byok.description: How this agent uses the workspace's own provider keys (Bring your own keys). `null` (or `workspace`) follows the workspace: its default scope applies when it brings its own keys. `off` never does: our voices and models at our normal pricing, whatever the workspace does, and the model is not held to the voice-only-BYOK model list. `all`, `voice`, `llm` or `llm_voice` runs this agent on that scope's keys whatever the workspace default is; refused with `409` naming the missing key unless the workspace holds verified keys for every kind that scope needs. If a key goes later, the agent falls back to the workspace's scope at the next call. Omit the field to leave it unchanged; saved BYOK model and voice choices are kept but not used while it is `off`. Read back as `workspace` when it follows the workspace.

collectFields.description: The details it fills in after every call, in the shape a call's `extract` takes. Empty when it collects nothing.

webKey.description: The public key the website widget embeds (`pk_…`). It is published on your site, so it is not a secret.

items.description: The agents on this page, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

AgentEscalation.description: When the agent hands the conversation to a person on your team.

onNoAnswer.description: Hand over when it cannot answer.

onRequest.description: Hand over when the customer asks for a person.

AgentStep.description: One step of the conversation script.

title.description: What the step is for, up to 80 characters.

detail.description: What the agent should do here, up to 600 characters.

branches.description: Conditions within the step, as written. Empty when it has none.

action.description: What to do when it holds.

collect.description: What must be in hand before the step is done. Empty when nothing is.

accent.description: The accent colour as `#rrggbb`, or null for the default.

height.description: The open widget's height in pixels.

welcomeScreen.description: Whether the widget opens on a welcome screen before the chat.

welcomeCollectLeads.description: Whether the welcome screen asks for the visitor's details.

answersCalls.description: Whether the agent takes calls at all.

surfaces.description: Where it answers calls: a phone number, the call button on your website, WhatsApp calls. A new agent starts with `["web", "whatsapp"]`, and `phone` is added when a number is attached. Set it with `voice.surfaces`.

voice.description: The voice id from List Voices it speaks with.

phoneNumber.description: The number it answers on, or null. Read-only.

language.description: The language for calls, or null to follow the agent's `language`.

summariseCalls.description: Whether a summary is written after every call.

detectMachines.description: Whether it hangs up on an answering machine.

recordDoNotCall.description: Whether the agent can add a caller to your do-not-call list when they ask not to be called again. True unless switched off.

maxCallSeconds.description: The longest a call may run, in seconds; null for the default ceiling of 20 minutes.

ringSeconds.description: How long a call the agent places rings before it is given up; 30 unless set. A call nobody answers in that time ends as `no_answer`.

pastConversations.description: What a call does with earlier conversations: `quiet` uses them without mentioning it, `recap` opens by recapping them, `fresh` uses nothing from before.

unavailableMessage.description: What a caller hears when this agent's line is switched off, or null for the standard sentence.

unavailableMessageNote.description: Set when the saved message will not always be spoken as written: a message is read aloud only on Plivo numbers (English, or English in Roman letters) and Twilio numbers (English and Hindi), and in no other script — callers then hear the standard sentence. Numbers with other providers, and WhatsApp calling, never speak a message; that is not flagged here. The message itself is kept. Null when it is read as written, or there is no message.

callStartUrl.description: Where an inbound call asks your system who is calling before the agent answers, or null. See `callStartUrl` on the input for the request and the answer.

callStartSecret.description: The secret that signs call-start lookups. Present ONLY on the response to the request that set a new `callStartUrl` — store it now; it is never shown again. Setting a different address creates a new one.

thinking.description: Whether it says a short filler while a reply is slow. Default true.

thinkingLines.description: Your own filler lines. Empty means the built-in ones, in the caller's language.

thinkingDelayMs.description: Milliseconds of quiet before a filler. 900 unless set.

thinkingRepeatMs.description: Milliseconds before another filler may follow. 2500 unless set.

thinkingAtTurnEnd.description: Whether it acknowledges before every reply. Default false.

turnDetection.description: How the agent decides the caller has finished speaking: `smart`, `timer`, `timer_v2` or `ear`, or null when it follows the platform's own setting (the Voice page shows which). Reads null until you choose one.

turnSilenceSeconds.description: Seconds of quiet that end the caller's turn, or null for the default (0.25 s on most lines). In `smart` it is a ceiling on how long the model may keep waiting (0.6 s when null). Reads null until you set a number.

reaskAfterSeconds.description: How long the agent waits, after a question it asked has had no answer, before it asks again: 1.5 to 10 seconds, `0` for never, or null for the platform's 2.5 seconds.

interruptWords.description: Words a caller must say to cut the agent off mid-sentence. 3 unless set.

neverInterrupt.description: Whether the agent can never be cut off. Default false.

realtimeVoice.description: Only for an agent on a realtime model (OpenAI GPT-Live-1 or OpenAI GPT-Realtime Mini): one of that model's own voices, from `voices` on its entry in List Models. null is its default. The agent's `voice` is kept as it is, for when it goes back to another model. Realtime models are on the Enterprise plan only for now: we set them up on your agents, they are not in List Models, and `model` refuses one as a new choice.

realtimeSession.description: OpenAI GPT-Realtime Mini's session settings (the Playground's Realtime session). Every field, with its value or default; ignored on any other model.

noiseReduction.description: Cleans the caller's audio first. `auto`: near_field on phone calls, far_field on web calls. Default auto.

turnDetection.description: How it knows the caller has finished: `server_vad` by silence, `semantic_vad` by meaning. Default server_vad.

vadThreshold.description: By silence: how loud speech must be to count. Default 0.5.

prefixPaddingMs.description: By silence: audio kept from just before speech starts, ms. Default 300.

silenceDurationMs.description: By silence: the quiet that ends the caller's turn, ms. Default 500.

idleTimeoutMs.description: By silence: after this much quiet the agent speaks up, ms; null is never (the default). Five quiet minutes from the caller still end the call.

eagerness.description: By meaning: how soon it decides the caller has finished. Default auto.

interruptResponse.description: Whether a caller speaking cuts the agent off. Default true.

transcriptionModel.description: The caller's transcript: fast (the default), most accurate, or classic.

transcriptionPrompt.description: Names and brand words the transcript should get right; null is none.

maxOutputTokens.description: The longest single reply, in tokens; null is unlimited (the default).

truncationRetention.description: On a long call, the share of the conversation kept when it is trimmed; null lets the model decide (the default).

earlyAnswers.description: On by default. The agent starts working on its reply the moment it has heard what the caller said, while it is still making sure they have finished, so the first words come sooner. If the caller goes on, that early reply is thrown away and never spoken or recorded, but it still costs the model's tokens: on an agent that runs on your own model key they are billed to your key and are not counted in the call's `usage`. `false` starts a reply only once the caller has finished.

holdShortSpeech.description: Whether words too short to cut in are kept and answered when it stops. Default true.

greetingUninterruptible.description: Whether the greeting plays to the end on phone calls. Default false.

openingWaitsForCaller.description: Whether the opening line waits for the person who picked up to speak first. Default false: it plays the moment the call connects. true: it plays right after their first words (a "Hello") or, if they stay silent, after four seconds. Phone calls on a voice agent; not used on a realtime model.

openingWaitSeconds.description: Seconds of silence after which a held opening line plays anyway (only with `openingWaitsForCaller`). 4 unless set.

ambience.description: A background sound under the call, or null for none.

ambienceVolume.description: The background sound's volume. 0.15 unless set.

speakingSpeed.description: How fast the agent talks, as a multiple of the voice's own pace. 1 unless set; 0.9 is a little slower.

backchannelDetection.description: Ear mode only. Whether the agent tells a caller's backchannel ("haan ji", "okay", "mm-hmm") from a real interruption while it is talking. On unless set to false.

backchannelWords.description: Ear mode only. Caller backchannel words that always mean "I am listening" for this agent, on top of what the agent recognises. Empty is the agent's own judgement alone.

acknowledgements.description: Ear mode only. Whether the agent speaks a short backchannel / acknowledgement while the caller pauses mid-explanation. On unless set to false; it is not part of the conversation record.

acknowledgementWords.description: Ear mode only. The agent's backchannel phrases, said in turn. Empty is a short word in the caller's own language.

vocabulary.description: Names and terms the agent should hear correctly on calls: products, places, people. Empty is none.

endCallOnFinish.description: Whether the line is released when the agent ends the conversation. A new agent starts with it off; an agent made earlier that never had it saved reads as true.

nudgeAfterSeconds.description: Seconds of silence before it asks whether the caller is still there, or null to never ask.

nudges.description: How many times it asks. 1 unless set.

nudgePhrase.description: What it asks, or null for the built-in question in the caller's language.

endAfterSilenceSeconds.description: Seconds of silence after which the call ends, or null, as you set it. On a call the hang-up is never earlier than the last question allows (`nudgeAfterSeconds × (nudges + 1)`), so a call can run longer than this number says.

endPhrases.description: Phrases that end the call when the caller says them, stored lower-case without punctuation.

callInstructions.description: How it should speak on calls, or null for the built-in call rules.

AgentCollectField.description: One detail the agent fills in after every call.

name.description: The field's key in each call's results.

description.description: What to put in it, as the model reads it.

choices.description: The values a text field must be one of, or null.

AgentEscalationInput.description: When the agent hands over to a person. Send either or both.

onNoAnswer.description: Hand over when it cannot answer.

onRequest.description: Hand over when the customer asks for a person.

AgentStepInput.description: One step of the script. A step with neither a title nor a detail is dropped.

title.description: What the step is for. Trimmed and cut to 80 characters.

detail.description: What the agent should do here. Trimmed and cut to 600 characters.

branches.description: Conditions within the step, e.g. when `If they are already a customer`, action `skip to payment`. A branch missing either half is dropped. Returned in `steps` as written.

action.description: What to do when it holds.

collect.description: What must be in hand before the step is done — a name, a date, an order number. Returned in `steps`.

example.title: Budget and size
example.detail: Ask for their budget and whether they want a 2 BHK or a 3 BHK.

AgentWidgetInput.description: The website widget's look. Send any subset.

theme.description: The widget's design. Anything else is refused with a 400.

accent.description: A colour as `#rrggbb` or `#rgb` (the `#` optional). Null or an empty string clears it to the default; anything else that is not a colour is refused with a 400.

welcomeScreen.description: Open the widget on a welcome screen — here, where it is returned, or top-level as before.

welcomeCollectLeads.description: Ask for the visitor's details on the welcome screen — here or top-level.

height.description: The open widget's height in pixels, clamped to 420–900.

AgentVoiceInput.description: How the agent handles calls. Send any subset. Where an agent has no voice channel yet, sending any of these creates one — switched OFF, so setting only a voice or a message never starts it taking calls; send `answersCalls: true` to switch it on.

answersCalls.description: Whether the agent takes calls at all.

voice.description: A voice id from List Voices. A Studio voice needs the Pro plan or above. `null` puts the agent back on the default voice a new agent starts with (currently Kavya, a Premium voice, which bills at the Premium rate) — the way back to the defaults. An empty string is refused with a 400.

language.description: The language for calls: one the console offers, by its English name (`Hindi`) or its tag (`hi-IN`), or null to follow the agent's `language`. Anything else, `auto` included, is refused with a 400.

summariseCalls.description: Write a summary after every call (a small charge per call).

detectMachines.description: Hang up on an answering machine.

recordDoNotCall.description: Let the agent add a caller to your do-not-call list when they ask not to be called again. On by default; `false` takes the ability away from this agent, and numbers you add yourself (API, Contacts page) are unaffected. In the console: Voice page, Do-not-call list.

maxCallSeconds.description: The longest a call may run, in whole seconds; null for the default ceiling of 20 minutes.

ringSeconds.description: How long a call the agent places (API calls, campaigns, callbacks, test calls) rings before it is given up, in whole seconds (10 to 60); `null` for the default of 30. In the console: Voice page, Ring time. A call nobody answers in that time ends as `no_answer` (the `hangup` of `call.completed`), and a campaign retries it as one. Can be set per call on Place Call.

pastConversations.description: What a call does with earlier conversations: `quiet` (the default) uses them without mentioning it, `recap` opens by recapping them and asking whether to carry on, `fresh` uses nothing from before.

unavailableMessage.description: What a caller hears when this agent's line is switched off (`answersCalls` false), instead of the standard "not taking calls" sentence. Trimmed, control characters removed, 300 characters at most (longer is a 400, not a cut); null or blank clears it. Phone calls only. Spoken on Plivo numbers (English, or English in Roman letters, but not Hindi) and on Twilio numbers (English and Hindi); a Vobiz number gets no message (the call is declined as before), a Telnyx number a busy tone and WhatsApp calling a rejection. It is read by the provider's own Indian-English voice, so a message in any other script, or Hindi on Plivo, plays the standard sentence instead. The message is kept either way, and `unavailableMessageNote` says when it will not be spoken as written. Never used for a call refused over a plan, a balance or busy lines.

callStartUrl.description: A call-start lookup: an https address of yours, asked who is calling when an inbound phone or WhatsApp call is about to be answered by the agent (not one forwarded to a person), before the agent speaks. We POST `{ "event": "call.started", "callId", "surface": "phone" | "whatsapp", "agentId", "from", "to", "direction": "inbound", "contact", "sentAt" }` — `to` is the agent's voice line (also on a WhatsApp call), and `contact` is the contact you hold under the caller's number (`id`, `name`, `phone`, `email`, `externalId`) or null — signed like a webhook (`x-thinnest-signature`, and `x-thinnest-signature-v2` over `<x-thinnest-delivered-at>.<body>`) with the secret returned once as `voice.callStartSecret`. Answer within 2 seconds with `{ "variables": { "name": "Asha", "plan": "Gold" } }`: up to 20, names normalised and values cut to 150 characters as for Place Call's `variables`, strings, numbers and booleans only. They fill `{{...}}` placeholders in the greeting and instructions, over the contact's own fields (yours win). No answer in 2 seconds, a non-2xx status or anything else, and the call goes ahead without them; we never retry it, but the phone provider asks again if it did not get our answer in time, and that repeats the request with the same `callId`, so dedupe on `callId`. Must be https, not a private address, and carry no username or password. `null` or an empty string switches it off and deletes the secret; a new address creates a new secret. Refused with `503` `signing_unavailable` while call-start requests cannot be signed (try again later).

callStartSecret.description: Send `"rotate"` to create a new signing secret for the existing `callStartUrl` (or the one in the same request); the old one stops working at once. The new secret comes back once, as `voice.callStartSecret` on the response. Needs a `callStartUrl`. You cannot choose the secret yourself.

surfaces.description: Where the agent answers calls: `web` (the call button on your website), `whatsapp` (WhatsApp calls; whether a WhatsApp number takes calls is its own Calls switch on Connect WhatsApp), `phone` (its phone number). A new agent starts with `["web", "whatsapp"]`, and `phone` is added when a number is attached. Adding `phone` while the agent answers calls (`answersCalls` true) and has no number to answer or call from is refused with `409` `phone_number_required`; with calls off you may set it first and attach a number after. On a plan that cannot hold a number, `phone` is left out. While a number is attached, `phone` stays on even if you leave it out (a number nobody answers is a caller hearing silence): to stop the phone ringing, send `answersCalls: false` or take the number off. Anything other than these three values is a 400.

thinking.description: Say a short filler ("One moment.") when a reply has not started after `thinkingDelayMs`, for example while an action runs.

thinkingLines.description: Your own filler lines, one phrase per item: up to 8, each 60 characters or fewer after trimming (blank items are dropped; a line break inside an item is a 400). Longer or more is refused with a 400, never cut. Each call uses the lines written in the caller's script (Hindi lines on a Hindi call, English on an English one). Words of an Indian language typed in Roman letters are converted to that language's script when saved. `null` or `[]` goes back to the built-in fillers in the caller's language.

thinkingDelayMs.description: Milliseconds of quiet before the filler is said, 200 to 5000. `null` goes back to 900.

thinkingRepeatMs.description: Milliseconds after one filler before another may be said (and how often a long-running action is covered again), 1000 to 10000. `null` goes back to 2500.

thinkingAtTurnEnd.description: Always acknowledge ("Okay.") the moment the caller stops, before every reply, instead of only when a reply is slow. Suits a slow model; on a quick one it is a syllable in front of everything.

turnDetection.description: How the agent decides the caller has finished speaking. `smart`: a model predicts whether the sentence is finished, so a caller who pauses to think is not cut off, but replies start later; `turnSilenceSeconds` is then a ceiling on how long it keeps waiting (0.6 s unless set). `timer`: a stretch of silence ends the turn, which is faster but cuts off people who pause mid-sentence; `turnSilenceSeconds` is that silence (0.25 s unless set). `timer_v2`: like `timer`, but at each pause an AI check reads what the caller said and decides whether they have finished, so a pause mid-sentence is not answered as if they were done; words said over the agent are judged the same way (a listener's "haan ji" lets it carry on, a clear interruption stops it); `turnSilenceSeconds` is not used. `ear`: real-time speech recognition decides when the caller has finished, and can stop the agent while the caller is still speaking; the agent uses `timer` on a line where real-time recognition is not available. `null` follows the platform's own setting (the Voice page shows which). Anything else is a 400.

turnSilenceSeconds.description: Seconds of quiet, 0.2 to 3. With `turnDetection` `timer` it is the silence that ends the caller's turn (0.25 s unless set); with `smart` it is a ceiling on how long the model may keep waiting (0.6 s unless set). `null` goes back to the default. Shorter answers sooner and cuts slow speakers off more often.

reaskAfterSeconds.description: How long to wait, after a question the agent asked has had no answer, before it asks again. `0` means never ask again; otherwise 1.5 to 10 seconds (one decimal). `null` goes back to the platform's 2.5 seconds.

interruptWords.description: How many words a caller must say to cut the agent off while it is speaking, 1 to 6. Short acknowledgements ("okay", "haan") under this never interrupt. `null` goes back to 3.

neverInterrupt.description: The agent can never be cut off, on any line, at any length — for a disclosure or a price read out in full. What the caller says meanwhile is handled by `holdShortSpeech`.

realtimeVoice.description: Only for an agent on a realtime model (OpenAI GPT-Live-1 or OpenAI GPT-Realtime Mini): one of that model's own voices, from `voices` on its entry in List Models. null is its default. The agent's `voice` is kept as it is, for when it goes back to another model. Realtime models are on the Enterprise plan only for now: we set them up on your agents, they are not in List Models, and `model` refuses one as a new choice.

realtimeSession.description: Only for an agent on OpenAI GPT-Realtime Mini: its session settings. Send only the fields you change; the rest keep their values. null puts them all back to the defaults. A value outside its range is brought into it; a wrong type or an unknown field is refused, naming it.

noiseReduction.description: Cleans the caller's audio first. `auto`: near_field on phone calls, far_field on web calls. Default auto.

CallBilling.description:
What the call was billed as. Null for a booked call that has not rung.

**Carrier-only calls.** A call that ended before the agent spoke runs no agent (no recogniser, model or voice), so it is charged the phone carrier's fee only: ₹0.38 a minute in INR, charged in 30-second blocks (₹0.19 each; in USD at our conversion rate). `billedSeconds` is the length rounded up to the block. For these calls `voicePlan` and `ratePerMinuteMicro` still show the plan and rate the call was set up on, which is not what was charged: reconcile such a call by `costMicro`.

**A call that ends at 0 seconds** is not charged at all: `billedSeconds` stays null. One that lasts a second is one 30-second block.

**Forwarded calls are not carrier-only.** A call forwarded to a phone (`forwardedTo`) on a number rented here is billed for every second the caller was connected, at the rate it was admitted at: the voice plan of the agent attached to the number, or the Premium plan when no agent is. When your own keys apply (the agent's, or the workspace's when no agent is attached), that is the flat own-key price of the set instead (`voicePlan` is null), even though the forward uses none of your keys. On a number you brought nothing is charged: `ratePerMinuteMicro` still shows the rate the call was admitted at, and `billedSeconds` is null.

**Free trial calls.** `voicePlan`, `ratePerMinuteMicro` and `billedSeconds` are null for a call paid from a free-plan workspace's trial minutes. A call in a workspace on a paid plan, a developer's own test calls included, is billed from its balance and carries them.

billedOn.description: `usage` for a call on a realtime (speech-to-speech) model, OpenAI GPT-Live-1: it is charged at that model's own flat rate a minute with the phone line included, per second on web and in 30-second blocks on phone (`billedSeconds`), so `voicePlan` and `ratePerMinuteMicro` are null and `chargedMicro` is the charge. `plan` for every other call.

chargedMicro.description: What a call billed on usage was charged, in millionths of `currency`, at a white-label reseller's price for its clients. Null on a call billed on a plan, and until a usage call has been charged.

keys.description: Whose keys the call ran on, as it was set up when the call started: `off` for ours; `all` your speech recognition, model and voice; `voice` your voice only; `llm` your model only; `llm_voice` your model and voice.

voicePlan.description: The voice plan the call was priced on (`off` and `llm` calls). `standard` appears only on calls before 23 October 2026, when standard voices were retired. Null for the flat own-key prices (`all`, `voice`, `llm_voice`), for a free trial call, and for calls before 15 October 2026.

ratePerMinuteMicro.description: The per-minute price the call was charged at, fixed when it started, in millionths of `currency` (2000000 is 2.00) — at a white-label reseller's price for its clients. A call is charged in 30-second steps (a WhatsApp call by the minute) at half of this each. Null for a free trial call.

billedSeconds.description: The seconds the charge was for: the call's length rounded up to its step, or to the phone carrier's block for a call that ended before the agent spoke (charged the carrier's fee only). Null until a charge was taken — a call still live, a free trial call, and calls settled before 15 October 2026.

currency.description: The currency the rate is in, as `currency` on the call.

turns.description: Caller turns the agent answered. A turn that got no reply (an echo of the agent's own voice, a turn after it hung up) is not counted.

responseMs.description: How long the caller waited: from when they stopped speaking to the agent's first audio on the line. Null when it was not measured.

median.description: Half the turns were faster than this, in milliseconds.

p90.description: Nine turns in ten were at least this fast, in milliseconds.

answerMs.description: How long the caller waited for the first word of the ACTUAL answer: from when they stopped speaking to that word being heard. `responseMs` stops at the first sound of any kind, so a thinking line or an acknowledgement that plays first ends it; this does not. When a thinking line spoke first the answer's start is worked out from the audio queued behind it (the turn's `answerAudioEstimated` in Get Call Timeline says so). Only turns that had answer words count. Null when it was not measured, and on calls from before it was recorded.

median.description: Half the turns were faster than this, in milliseconds.

p90.description: Nine turns in ten were at least this fast, in milliseconds.

firstTokenMs.description: Our side of that wait: from the turn reaching the model to its first word. Null when it was not measured.

median.description: Half the turns were faster than this, in milliseconds.

p90.description: Nine turns in ten were at least this fast, in milliseconds.

longSilences.description: Silences, on either side, at least `longSilenceSeconds` long.

longestSilenceSeconds.description: The longest stretch where nobody spoke.

interruptions.description: Times the caller started speaking while the agent was talking.

knowledgeTurns.description: Turns where the agent looked something up in its knowledge: its own search, or passages handed to it up front. Null when this count was not available for the call.

modelErrors.description: Turns where the agent could not get an answer and apologised to the caller instead. Null when this count was not available for the call.

error.description: Why the call could not be called off.

offset.description: Whole seconds from the start of the call to `at` — for order and rough position, not audio sync.

turnDecidedMs.description: The turn was decided and an answer was wanted.

answerTextMs.description: The first words of the answer left the model. A thinking line is not the answer.

It rings for 30 seconds. If nobody picks up, a caller on a number from us, Plivo or Twilio hears that nobody could take the call; a caller on a number brought from Telnyx gets no spoken message — the line rings out or returns busy, then ends. A call that is picked up is cut off at its limit: on a number rented here, when the balance can no longer pay for it and never later than 20 minutes (the platform's maximum call length); on a number you brought, after 30 minutes. Premium-rate, shared-cost, toll-free, satellite and some high-cost international destinations are refused (`forward_destination_not_allowed`, 422). It works whether or not an agent answers the number: with an agent, the forward replaces it; with none (never attached, deleted, or its voice switched off) the forward answers the call itself, so the number never goes quiet. A workspace that cannot pay for a call, or has no free call line, does not forward - the caller hears that the number is not answering. Billed like a call put through to a person: every connected minute on a number rented here (at the voice plan of the agent attached to the number, or the Premium plan when no agent is; under your own keys, the flat own-key price of that set), nothing on a number you brought.
