WhatsAppTemplate.description: A WhatsApp template, with what a send needs from it.

name.description: The template's name — what Send Message and Create Campaign take.

language.description: Its language code.

category.description: WhatsApp's category, which decides its price and its rules.

status.description: `draft` until submitted, `pending` while WhatsApp reviews it, then `approved` or `rejected`. WhatsApp may later `pause` an approved template that recipients flag. Only `approved` can be sent.

agent.description: The agent the template belongs to (`ag_…`).

body.description: The message, with `{{1}}`, `{{2}}` … for the blanks. For an authentication template, the sentence WhatsApp writes around the code.

variableCount.description: How many body values a send must carry, in order: the highest `{{n}}` in the body.

variableLabels.description: The example given for each body blank.

buttonVariableCount.description: How many button values a send must carry: one per link button whose address ends in a blank.

headerKind.description: The header. `image`, `video` or `document` means a send must pass a media link for it.

agentMaySend.description: Whether an agent may send this template during a call or chat (its `send_whatsapp` tool). Only a Utility template with no blank in a link button can be. Every language of a name agrees. Change it with Update Template, sending `agentMaySend` alone.

kind.description: `url`, `phone`, `quick_reply`, `copy_code`, or `flow` for a button made in the console that opens a WhatsApp form.

label.description: What the button says. Empty for `copy_code`, whose label WhatsApp writes.

url.description: A link button's address. A trailing `{{1}}` is filled per send.

WhatsAppTemplateDetail.description: A WhatsApp template with its parts and review note.

headerText.description: A text header's words. `null` for any other header.

footer.description: The footer line. Empty when there is none.

reviewNote.description: Why WhatsApp refused it, when it did. `null` otherwise.

WhatsAppTemplateSaved.description: The template, plus a sentence about what just happened.

message.description: What happened: saved as a draft, sent for review, or — with `submit: true` — saved as a draft with the reason the submission was refused.

items.description: Templates, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page. `null` on the last page.

WhatsAppTemplateHeader.description: The line or media above the body. `null` means no header.

text.description: A `text` header's words. Required for `text`; no placeholders.

mediaUrl.description: For `image`, `video` or `document`: an https link to an example file WhatsApp's reviewers can fetch. Required for those kinds.

WhatsAppTemplateButton.description: One button. A template takes at most three quick replies, two link buttons and one call button, and quick replies cannot be mixed with the other kinds.

kind.description: A link, a call, a quick reply, or a button that copies an offer code.

label.description: What the button says. Required for every kind but `copy_code`, whose label WhatsApp writes.

url.description: For `url`: an https address. It may end with one `{{1}}`, filled per send.

phone.description: For `phone`: the number in full international form, like `+919812345678`.

sample.description: For a `url` that ends in `{{1}}`: an example value for the reviewers. Required then.

code.description: For `copy_code`: the example coupon WhatsApp reviews the template against.

WhatsAppTemplateAuthApp.description: An Android app a one-tap code fills into.

WhatsAppTemplateAuth.description: An authentication template's settings. WhatsApp writes the message itself ("*123456* is your verification code."), so these are all you choose.

expiryMinutes.description: How long the code is valid, shown as "Expires in 10 minutes."

securityRecommendation.description: Adds "For your security, do not share this code."

otpType.description: `copy_code`: a button that copies the code. `one_tap`: fills it into your Android app, which needs `supportedApps`.

supportedApps.description: Required for `one_tap`: the apps the code fills into.

name.description: Lowercase letters, numbers and underscores only. Unique per language in your workspace.

language.description: A language WhatsApp templates support, such as `en`, `en_US` or `hi`.

category.description: `utility` for something the customer is expecting (an order or appointment update), `marketing` for promotions, `authentication` for one-time codes.

body.description: The message, with blanks numbered `{{1}}`, `{{2}}` … in order. A blank cannot be at the very start or end, two cannot sit next to each other, and there must be enough words around them. Required unless `category` is `authentication`, where WhatsApp writes the body.
body.example: Hello {{1}}, your Kesar Naturals order {{2}} is packed and on its way.

samples.description: One example value per body blank, in order. WhatsApp's reviewers read the template with these filled in, so every blank needs one.

footer.description: One line of small print, with no blanks. A marketing template needs a way to opt out — "Reply STOP to opt out" here, or a quick-reply button.

agent.description: The agent the template belongs to (`ag_…`). Leave it out for the agent on your connected WhatsApp number (or your oldest agent).

submit.description: `true` also sends it to WhatsApp for review, as Submit Template does. If that is refused, the draft is kept and `message` says why.

WhatsAppTemplateUpdate.description: Only the fields sent change; the rest keep their current values. The result must pass the same rules as Create Template.

name.description: A new name: lowercase letters, numbers and underscores only.

language.description: A new language code WhatsApp templates support, such as `en`, `en_US` or `hi`.

body.description: The new message, with `{{1}}`, `{{2}}` … for the blanks. Ignored for an authentication template.

samples.description: One example per body blank, in order. Leave it out to keep the current examples.

footer.description: The new footer. `null` or `""` removes it.

buttons.description: The full new list of buttons, replacing the old one. `null` or `[]` removes them all.

agentMaySend.description: Let an agent send this template during a call or chat, or stop it. Send it **alone**, not with other fields; it applies to every language of the name, only a Utility template whose link buttons are fixed can be allowed, and it needs a **full** key because it decides what an agent may message customers with.

name.description: The placeholder's name, used as `{{name}}` in `url` and `bodyTemplate`: lower case letters, numbers and underscores, starting with a letter (3 to 40 characters).

description.description: What the value is. The model fills it from the conversation using this alone — never leave it vague.

required.description: Whether the agent must have this value before it may call.

agent.description: The agent it belongs to (`ag_…`).

name.description: The tool name the agent sees.

description.description: When the agent should call it.

url.description: The `https://` address, with `{{placeholders}}` — declared parameters, or the platform's dotted ones such as `{{call.id}}`. The host must be written out: no placeholder before the path.

parameters.description: What the agent fills in.

bodyTemplate.description: The JSON body sent, with quoted placeholders; null for none.

headerNames.description: The names of the headers sent. Their values are write-only and never returned.

speakBefore.description: On calls, what the agent says while your API is being called.

speakAfter.description: On calls, what the agent says while it turns your answer into a reply.

enabled.description: Whether the agent may call it. A new action is always `false`.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

name.description: The tool name the agent sees: 3 to 40 characters, lower case letters, numbers and underscores, starting with a letter. It cannot be one of the agent's built-in tools, and must be unique on this agent.

description.description: When the agent should call it, in a sentence (at least 10 characters). The model decides from this alone.

url.description: An `https://` address, with `{{placeholders}}` for parameters. Every placeholder needs a parameter of that name. Addresses inside private networks are refused when called.

method.description: The HTTP method; any case is accepted.

parameters.description: Up to 20 values the agent fills from the conversation. Names must be unique.

bodyTemplate.description: A JSON body with **quoted** placeholders, e.g. `{"id": "{{order_id}}"}`. It must still be valid JSON once the blanks are filled.

headers.description: Up to 10 headers, name to value — typically `Authorization`. **Write-only:** sealed on arrival; only their names come back, as `headerNames`. Blank values are dropped.

speakBefore.description: On calls, what the agent says while your API is being called.

speakAfter.description: On calls, what the agent says while it turns your answer into a reply.

UpdateHttpActionRequest.description: Any field `POST` takes, plus `enabled`. Send at least one. The result is validated as it will be saved: a new `url` is checked against the parameters already there.

name.description: The tool name the agent sees; same rules as on create.

description.description: When the agent should call it (at least 10 characters).

url.description: An `https://` address with `{{placeholders}}`.

parameters.description: Replaces the whole list.

bodyTemplate.description: The JSON body; null removes it.

headers.description: Leave it out (or send `{}`) to keep the saved headers. Sending any **replaces the whole set**, so include every header the call needs. There is no way to remove all headers short of deleting the action.

speakBefore.description: What the agent says while your API is called; null clears it.

speakAfter.description: What the agent says afterwards; null clears it.

enabled.description: `true` puts the action within reach of every conversation the agent has; `false` takes it away.

arguments.description: Parameter name to value — what the agent would have filled in.

ok.description: Whether your API answered with a success status.

status.description: Your API's HTTP status; `0` when the call could not be made at all (a blocked address, a timeout).

result.description: What the agent would have read: your answer summarised to about 4,000 characters, or why the call failed.

summary.description: What it does, in one sentence.

switchable.description: Whether `PATCH` may switch it. `search_knowledge` is not a switch: it is on whenever the agent has knowledge.

reachesOtherChannels.description: Whether it contacts the customer on another channel (a call, a WhatsApp, an email).

ready.description: Only on the three tools that reach other channels: on **and** what it needs exists, so it will really attach.

needs.description: Only on the three tools that reach other channels: what must also be true, in plain words.

agent.description: The agent (`ag_…`).

webSearch.description: Searching the web. Shown, never switchable here.

recall.description: How much of a recognised customer's history from other channels the agent may use.

verifyByCode.description: Whether a customer is confirmed with a one-time WhatsApp code rather than their email.

knowledgeOnCalls.description: Whether the agent searches its knowledge during phone and web calls. On unless you switch it off; chat is not affected.

handOver.description: How a hand-over to a person happens.

mode.description: `chat` flags the conversation for your team; `call` also puts a caller through to `phone`.

phone.description: The number callers are put through to, in E.164.

line.description: What the agent says before putting a caller through.

transferMode.description: How a caller is put through to `phone`. `cold` (the default): the phone rings and the caller is connected when someone answers. `warm`: the person who answers first hears a short spoken summary of the call, then the caller is connected; the caller hears ringing meanwhile.

acceptKey.description: Warm transfers only: `true` (the default) connects the caller only after the person presses 1, so a voicemail never takes the call — not pressed in time counts as not answered. `false` connects as soon as the summary has played. Press 1 works on Plivo numbers only for now.

agents.description: Other agents a call may be handed to mid-call, in order. Empty when none.

agent.description: The agent's id, `ag_…`.

name.description: Its name, which is what the model picks it by.

when.description: When to hand over to it.

mode.description: `warm` (the default): the other agent gets a short summary and the conversation, and opens by saying who it is and why the caller is there. `cold`: it does not see the conversation so far and greets the caller as on a new call.

messages.description: Notes from the changes applied, in order; often empty.

UpdateAgentBuiltInToolsRequest.description: Send at least one field. Changes apply in order (tools, recall, verifyByCode, knowledgeOnCalls, handOver) and stop at the first refusal; what came before it is kept, and the refusal says so.

tools.description: Tool id to `true` or `false`. Switchable: `capture_lead`, `escalate_to_human`, `schedule_callback`, `call_them_now`, `send_whatsapp`, `send_sms`, `reply_by_email`.

recall.description: How much of a recognised customer's history the agent may use: `trusted` (all of it), `two_tier` (the default) or `verified` (only once they are confirmed).

verifyByCode.description: Confirm a customer with a one-time WhatsApp code instead of their email.

knowledgeOnCalls.description: Let the agent search its knowledge during calls (on by default). Off, a call answers from its instructions alone and skips the search; chat is not affected.

handOver.description: Fields you leave out keep their saved value.

mode.description: `chat` or `call`. A call needs a `phone` (sent now or already saved).

phone.description: The number to put callers through to, with its country code. Null clears it.

line.description: What the agent says before putting a caller through. Null clears it.

transferMode.description: `cold` or `warm`. Warm: the person who answers first hears a short spoken summary of the call, then the caller is connected.

acceptKey.description: Warm transfers: `true` waits for the person to press 1 before connecting the caller; `false` connects after the summary. Press 1 works on Plivo numbers only for now: saving `warm` with `acceptKey: true` on an agent whose number is on Telnyx is refused with a 400.

agents.description: Other agents in this workspace a call may be handed to mid-call, on phone and web calls (in the console: the agent's Actions page, Hand calls to another agent). Replaces the saved list; `[]` or null clears it. Each must answer calls (voice switched on). The call stays on the same line and conversation and runs as that agent from the caller's next words; the voice stays the call's own. At most 3 hand-offs per call, and never back to an agent already on it.

agent.description: The agent's id, `ag_…`. Not this agent.

when.description: When to hand over to it, for the agent to read — "the caller has a problem with an order they already placed".

mode.description: `warm` or `cold`. Warm: the other agent gets a short summary and the conversation and introduces itself. Cold: it starts without the conversation and greets the caller as on a new call. Left out: an agent already on the list keeps its saved mode, a new one is warm.

name.description: The tool's name, as the server lists it.

description.description: The server's own description of it; empty when it gave none.

enabled.description: Whether the agent may call it. Every tool arrives off.

name.description: Your name for it.

url.description: Its `https://` address.

signIn.description: `token` for a server reached with a header you sent; `browser` for one signed in through the console.

kind.description: `server` for a tool server; `store` for a store connection made in the console, whose tools are a fixed list.

authHeaderName.description: The header the token is sent in.

hasSecret.description: Whether a token is held. The token itself is never returned.

status.description: `connected` once it answered with its tools; `failed` when it could not be reached (see `lastError`); `pending` before the first answer.

lastSyncedAt.description: When it last listed its tools.

tools.description: What it offers, by name.

nextCursor.description: Always null: every server comes in one page.

message.description: What happened — how many tools were found, or why it could not be reached.

name.description: Your name for it, 2 to 200 characters.

url.description: Its `https://` address. It must be publicly reachable: private and internal addresses are refused.

authHeaderName.description: The header to send the token in, e.g. `Authorization`. Required when `secret` is sent.

secret.description: The header's value, e.g. `Bearer …`. **Write-only:** sealed on arrival; responses say only `hasSecret`.

enabled.description: `true` lets the agent call this tool in every conversation; `false` takes it away.

id.description: The tool's id, used as the key in `PATCH` `tools` and `phrases`.

writes.description: Whether calling it changes something in the account.

enabled.description: Whether it is switched on. Every tool starts off.

phrases.description: On calls, what the agent says while the tool runs.

before.description: Said while it waits; one phrase per line.

ToolConnection.description: One account an agent can work in. Fields beyond the first few depend on the kind: a calendar has `timezone`; spreadsheets and CRMs have `target`, `match` and `variableColumns`; records has `fields`, `recordCount` and `link`; a helpdesk has only `account` and `enabled`. Credentials never appear.

name.description: Its display name.

signIn.description: How it is connected: `key` by `POST` with a key; `browser` through a consent screen in the console (the API cannot); `none` for records, which need no account.

available.description: Whether this deployment offers it at all.

signInPending.description: Browser sign-ins only: a sign-in was started in the console and not finished.

account.description: Who it is connected as: `{ email, name }`, or `{ host, email }` for a helpdesk.

name.description: The account's name.

lastError.description: Why the last attempt to use it failed.

mode.description: All but the calendar and helpdesks: `tool` saves during the conversation; `parser` reads the conversation afterwards.

runAsync.description: Grist only: answer before the save finishes.

target.description: Spreadsheets and CRMs: what it is pinned to, and that target's real columns. Grist `{ doc, table, columns }`; Google Sheets `{ spreadsheet, sheet, columns }`; Zoho `{ module, columns }`.

match.description: Spreadsheets and CRMs: the column that finds a lead's existing row, or null to add a row per conversation.

variableColumns.description: Spreadsheets and CRMs: column to campaign variable.

tools.description: Its tools. Helpdesks have none here.

recordCount.description: Records only: how many records have been collected.

link.description: Records only: the link to read them. The passcode is shown only by the call that makes a link.

url.description: The link.

hasPasscode.description: Always true: the link needs its passcode.

passcode.description: Only in the response that made the link — never again.

enabled.description: Helpdesks only: whether it is in use.

items.description: Every kind, connected or not, in a fixed order.

toolsInUse.description: How many connection tools are switched on, across every connection.

maxTools.description: The most connection tools an agent may have on at once — one budget every connection shares.

toolsInUse.description: Connection tools switched on, across every connection.

inbound.description: Helpdesks only, and **only in this response**: paste both into the helpdesk's webhook so replies reach the agent.

url.description: The address the helpdesk should call.

secret.description: The secret it should sign with.

messages.description: What each applied change said, in order.

message.description: What happened, and what was kept.

apiKey.description: A live Cal.com API key (`cal_live_…`), from Settings → Developer → API keys. Write-only.
A Grist API key, from Account settings → Developer → API keys. Write-only.

fields.description: What to collect, one per entry — `Label` or `Label | what it means`. A string with one per line is accepted too.

subdomain.description: Just the subdomain — the `acme` in acme.zendesk.com.

email.description: The email address the API token belongs to.

clientSecret.description: The connected app's consumer secret. Write-only.

ConnectToolConnectionRequest.description: The body depends on `{kind}`. `googlesheets`, `zoho`, `zoho_bigin`, `hubspot` and `calendly` take no body here: they sign in through a browser in the console, and this answers `409`.

UpdateToolConnectionRequest.description: Any of these, as the kind allows. Applied in this order — fields, target, match, variableColumns, mode, runAsync, tools, phrases — stopping at the first refusal; what came before it is kept, and the refusal says so. Helpdesks (`zendesk`, `salesforce`) have nothing to configure.

fields.description: Records only: what to collect, `Label` or `Label | what it means`.

target.description: Spreadsheets, CRMs and Calendly: pins it and reads the target's real columns. Grist needs `doc` and `table`; Google Sheets `spreadsheet` and `sheet`; Zoho CRM, Bigin and HubSpot `module` (HubSpot's is `contacts`); Calendly `eventTypes`, the meeting types the agent may book. Use `GET …/options` to see the choices.

spreadsheet.description: Google Sheets: the spreadsheet id or link.

module.description: Zoho: the module's API name, e.g. `Leads`. HubSpot: `contacts`.

eventTypes.description: Calendly: the meeting type URIs the agent may book, from `GET …/options`.

properties.description: HubSpot only: the contact properties the agent fills and searches by (at most 40). Pinning starts from a default pick; this replaces it.

match.description: Spreadsheets and CRMs: fill the lead's existing row found by this column instead of adding one. Null (or `column: null`) adds a row per conversation.

column.description: A column of the pinned target.

type.description: `phone` compares numbers loosely; `exact` compares text exactly.

variableColumns.description: Spreadsheets and CRMs: column to campaign variable, e.g. `{ "Locality": "locality" }`. Neither may contain `=` or a line break. Replaces the saved map.

mode.description: All but the calendar: `tool` saves during the conversation; `parser` reads the conversation afterwards (and switches the save tool off).

runAsync.description: Grist only: answer before the save finishes.

tools.description: Tool id to `true` or `false`. Every id must be one of this connection's tools. Switching on counts against the shared `maxTools` budget.

phrases.description: Tool id to `{ before, after }`: what the agent says on a call while the tool runs. Up to 8 lines, each under 60 characters.

ToolConnectionOptions.description: What the account can reach, by kind.

name.description: The document's name.

plan.description: The account's plan, as Grist reports it.

modules.description: The modules the account can write to. HubSpot has one, `contacts`.

eventTypes.description: The account's active meeting types: `uri`, `name`, `minutes`, and `linkOnly` when the type asks required questions, so customers are sent a booking link for it instead of being booked directly.

url.description: The new link.

passcode.description: Its passcode — shown here and never again.

UsageSummary.description: Plan, replies this period, wallet and replies per day.

currency.description: The currency money is stated in.

period.description: The period `replies.used` counts: this calendar month in UTC.

start.description: Start of this calendar month, UTC.

replies.description: This period's replies against the plan's allowance.

included.description: Replies the plan includes this period; `null` when metered.

metered.description: `true`: every reply is paid from the wallet. `false`: an allowance of `included` replies.

stopped.description: `true` once a non-metered allowance is used up and replies have stopped.

billedTo.description: `developer` when this workspace is a developer's customer and its usage is billed to the developer; otherwise `self`.

wallet.description: The balance. `null` on Free (which has no wallet) and for a developer's customer (its developer pays).

daily.description: Replies per UTC day for the last `days`.

balanceMicro.description: The balance shown on the billing page. Integer micro-units of `currency`: 1000000 is one rupee or one dollar.

availableMicro.description: What can be spent now: the balance less money held for phone-number rent renewing soon. Integer micro-units of `currency`: 1000000 is one rupee or one dollar.

heldMicro.description: Money held for phone-number rent renewing soon. Integer micro-units of `currency`: 1000000 is one rupee or one dollar.

creditMicro.description: Plan credit included in the balance. Integer micro-units of `currency`: 1000000 is one rupee or one dollar.

creditExpiresAt.description: When the plan credit expires; `null` when there is none.

timezone.description: The clock the days are counted in. Always `UTC`, as on the Usage chart.

to.description: Last day counted (a `to` past today is cut to today).

days.description: Every day in the range, quiet days as zeros.

id.description: The call's id — the one `GET /calls/{id}` answers to: `out_…` for a call the API placed at once, `sch_…` for one the API scheduled or queued, and the call reference for any other (`web_…` for a website call, the carrier's own reference for a phone call). A call the API retried appears once per attempt, every attempt under the same id; `GET /calls/{id}` reports the latest.

status.description: The call's raw status, e.g. `completed`, `missed`, `failed`.

label.description: The same, in words, as the console shows it.

number.description: The other party's number; `null` on a web call.

from.description: Which of your numbers placed it, on an outbound call.

machine.description: `true` when an answering machine took the call.

agent.description: The agent on the call; `null` when none.

name.description: Agent name.

costMicro.description: What the workspace was charged for the call — a white-label client's at its reseller's price; `null` when nothing was charged. Integer micro-units of `currency`: 1000000 is one rupee or one dollar.

hasRecording.description: `true` when a recording exists and has not been deleted.

UsageCallList.description: A page of the call log, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page.

description.description: The row as the statement reads it: the note written at the charge, else the kind in words.

amountMicro.description: Signed: money in is positive, money out negative. Integer micro-units of `currency`: 1000000 is one rupee or one dollar.

balanceAfterMicro.description: The balance after this row. Integer micro-units of `currency`: 1000000 is one rupee or one dollar.

customer.description: For a developer: the customer workspace (`org_…`) this charge was for. Kept after the customer is erased.

UsageLedgerList.description: A page of the balance history, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page.

netMinor.description: Amount before tax, in minor units (paise, cents) of `currency`.

kind.description: The kind of tax charged, e.g. `igst`, or `null` when none.

gstin.description: The GSTIN the invoice was issued to, if any.

paymentRef.description: The payment's reference with the payment provider, for matching a bank statement.

UsageInvoiceList.description: A page of invoices, newest first.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page.

timezone.description: Days are UTC, as Settings → Developer counts the month.

totalMicro.description: Spend across all customers in the range. Integer micro-units of `currency`: 1000000 is one rupee or one dollar.

items.description: One per customer with charges in the range, biggest spend first.

name.description: Its name; `null` once erased.

externalId.description: Your own id for it, as set on `POST /customers`.

spendMicro.description: Spend, net of refunds. Integer micro-units of `currency`: 1000000 is one rupee or one dollar.

timezone.description: Your workspace's time zone, which buckets are in.

missed.description: Calls that never connected and were missed or completed unanswered.

failed.description: Calls that never connected and failed.

debitMicro.description: What the calls cost you (a white-label client's at its reseller's price). Integer micro-units of `currency`: 1000000 is one rupee or one dollar.

series.description: One bucket per hour or day, in your time zone.

bucket.description: Bucket start, local time without offset.

days.description: The rolling window, when asked by `days`. Absent with `from`/`to`.

sent.description: Messages sent by the agent or a person.

delivered.description: Sent messages whose latest receipt is delivered (not yet read).

noReceipt.description: Sent messages with no receipt yet.

errors.description: Failures by WhatsApp error code, most first.

cost.description: What the window's WhatsApp messages cost you, priced as the WhatsApp dashboard prices them.

totalMicro.description: What the messages cost you. Integer micro-units of `currency`: 1000000 is one rupee or one dollar.

complete.description: `false` when some messages are not priced yet, so `totalMicro` is a floor.

lines.description: The Usage page's WhatsApp table, row for row.

costMicro.description: Cost, micro-units; `null` with no rate card for that country (no debit was taken either).

wallet.description: The balance as the account card shows it. `null` on Free and for a developer's customer.

balanceMicro.description: Spendable balance. Integer micro-units of `currency`: 1000000 is one rupee or one dollar.

low.description: `true` when the console shows the balance as low.

knowledgeGaps.description: Questions the agent searched its knowledge for and found nothing — at most `rows`.

answerRate.description: Share of knowledge searches that found an answer; `null` with no searches.

PublicVoice.description: A voice an agent can speak with.

name.description: The voice's name.

accent.description: The accent it carries, as a language tag such as `hi` or `en-IN`.

tier.description: The picker's tab, and the rate a call is billed at. Never `standard`: standard voices were retired on 23 October 2026.

description.description: What it sounds like or is best for, when known.

mine.description: Present, and true, only on a voice your workspace cloned.

sharedFromDeveloper.description: Present, and true, only on a voice your DEVELOPER cloned, in a workspace that is one of its customers. Every clone a developer makes can be used on its customers' agents. Only the developer can rename or delete it (Update and Delete Voice Clone answer 404 for it here), and it counts against the developer's clone limit, not the customer's. If the developer deletes it, agents speaking with it move to a Premium voice.

WebhookPayload.description: What every delivery POSTs to an endpoint: the event's `id` (the same as `x-thinnest-event-id`, stable across retries), its name, when it happened, and its `data`. Ids inside `data` are the prefixed ids the API returns (`conv_…`, `cmp_…`, and `out_…`, `sch_…` or the call reference for a call). An endpoint with `includeCustomers` also gets `data.workspaceId` (`org_…`). One example per event follows.
